Entries.Text: No D3D11 device for the GPU texture encoder ({0}); BC6H/BC7 imports use the slower, lower quality CPU encoder.
Texture Import
Texture Import

Replace a texture's image, add textures, or replace every texture of the selected TPF that has an image with its name in a folder. DDS, PNG, TGA, TIFF, BMP, JPEG and WEBP files can be imported. Every import can be undone.
Select a TPF in the File List to import textures into it.
This TPF is for {0}. Only PC TPFs can be edited for now.
Selected Texture
The texture that Replace Selected Texture replaces, and which new textures are added after.
{0}: {1} x {2}, {3}, {4} mips, format byte {5}
No texture selected. New textures are added at the end of the TPF.
Format
The compression format the imported image is written in.
Keep the replaced texture's format
Keep the format of the texture being replaced (recommended: the game expects it), or choose one. When the format changes, the TPF format byte is set to the one the game uses for it.
Mip Maps
The smaller copies of the image used at a distance.
Match the replaced texture
Full chain
Top level only

Match: a texture with a full chain gets a full chain at the new size, one with fewer levels keeps its count. New textures get a full chain unless Top level only is chosen. A DDS file with the right format, size and mips is used as it is.
Size
The size of the imported image.
Resize to the replaced texture's size
Scale the imported image to the size of the texture it replaces. Off: the image keeps its own size. Block compressed formats need sizes divisible by 4.
Encoder
BC6H and BC7 are compressed on the GPU (DirectXTex with a D3D11 device). Other formats are compressed on the CPU.
BC6H/BC7 on the GPU: {0}
The GPU encoder starts with the first BC6H/BC7 import. Without a GPU, the quick CPU encoder is used.
Actions
Each action asks for the file or folder, encodes in the background, and applies as one undoable step.
Replace Selected Texture
Replace the selected texture's whole image with an image file. Its name, format byte and flags are kept. To change one icon of a sprite sheet, use Replace Selected Cells below.
Add Textures
Add one or more image files as new textures after the selected texture, named after the files.
Replace Matching Textures from Folder
Replace every texture of the selected TPF that has an image file with the same name in a folder (a .dds wins over other formats). Textures without a file are left as they are.
Progress
The import in progress, or the result of the last one.
Cancel
Stop the import. Nothing is applied.
Select the image to replace the texture with
Select the images to add
Select the folder with the replacement images

Replace from File
Replace this texture's image with an image file, using the Texture Import options.
Duplicate
Add a copy of this texture after it, named with a _copy suffix.
Delete
Remove this texture from the TPF. Materials that use its name will show a missing texture.
Add Textures from Files
Add one or more image files to this TPF as new textures, named after the files.
Replace Matching Textures from Folder
Texture Data
The selected texture's entry in the TPF. Each change is committed when the field loses focus, and can be undone.
Name
The texture's name. Materials find their textures by name, so renaming one breaks the materials that use it.
Format Byte
The TPF's format value for this texture. It should match the DDS format (for example 102 for BC7, 0 for BC1 in Elden Ring).
Flags
Unknown TPF flags: 0, 1, 2, 3 or 128 (0x80). 2 and 3 store the image compressed with DCP_EDGE.
Type
Texture, cubemap, volume or array; it comes from the image.
Mip Count
The TPF's mip count; it comes from the image.
Image Size
The size and mip levels in the image's DDS header.
Image Format
The DXGI format in the image's DDS header, and whether it uses a DX10 or a legacy (DXT1/DXT5/ATI) header.
Data Size
The size of the stored image.
Float Data (Unk00)
Extra values some textures carry (Dark Souls III and Bloodborne GI textures, Dark Souls II skies). Their meaning is unknown.
Float Data [{0}]
Layout Cells
This texture is a sprite sheet with a layout. These actions replace only the pixels of layout cells; the rest of the sheet keeps its exact bytes.
{0} cells selected: {1}
Select cells in the viewport or the Layout window to replace them.
Replace Selected Cells
Put an image file into the selected layout cells, scaled to each cell's size. Only the sheet's blocks under the cells are re-encoded; every other icon keeps its bytes. One undoable step.
Replace Cells from Folder

Put every image of a folder into the layout cell with its name (MENU_ItemIcon_00123.png goes into that cell, or a cell sharing its rectangle), all as one undoable step. Cells without a file are left as they are.
Select the image for the selected cells
Select the folder with images named after the cells
None of the {0} cells has an image with its name in {1}.
{0} changed while the cells were being encoded; nothing was applied. Try again.
New Cells
Add images to the sheet as new layout cells (e.g. new item icons). Each is placed in free space on whole blocks, so no other icon is re-encoded.
New cells: the image's size
New cells: the selected cell's size
The size of each new cell: the image's own size, or the size of the selected (or last) cell, the image scaled to it.
Grow the sheet when it is full
When a new cell doesn't fit, double the sheet (height first, up to 8192). The existing pixels are copied as they are; the atlas size in the layout follows.
Insert Images as New Cells
Add each image as a new cell named after its file (MENU_ItemIcon_12345.png), formatted like the selected (or last) cell, its pixels pasted into the sheet. One undoable step.

Rename TPF
The new name of {0}. Its folder and extension are kept. The game looks TPFs up by name, so a renamed TPF is only found by what refers to the new name.
Copied texture {0}.
Paste Textures
Paste the copied textures into this TPF, after the selected texture. Names in use get a number added.
Add Empty TPF
Add a new, empty TPF to this container after this one, made like it (platform, compression, layout).
Duplicate TPF
Add a copy of this TPF and all its textures after it, named with a _copy suffix.
Rename TPF
Change this TPF's name inside the container.
Delete TPF
Remove this TPF and its textures from the container.
Copy
Copy this texture, to paste it into another PC TPF (in any container or view).
Paste
Paste the copied textures after this one.
Copy As
Write a copy of this container, with any unsaved edits, into the project under a new name, e.g. c2010_h to c2011_h for a new character. Files inside that carry the old name are renamed too.
Copy Container As
The name of the copy of {0}. It is written to the same folder in the project, with the same extensions.
